_note: Paper trading only. CONSTITUTION.md section IV forbids real-money trading of any kind; this file describes a simulation and there is no code path from it to a broker. Every limit here is ENFORCED in code/paper-trading.js and covered by code/test-paper-trading.js -- the previous version of these rules lived only in knowledge/Guidelines.md as 'intended but not enforced', which is exactly the failure this replaces.
_riskPerTrade: Fraction of capital lost if a position is stopped out. Position size is DERIVED from this and the instrument's stop distance (maxPosition = riskPerTrade / stopLoss), so every instrument risks the same amount and the volatile ones simply get smaller positions.
_dailyLossLimit: Realized losses in one UTC day, as a fraction of starting capital. Opening is refused once breached.
_fallback: An instrument MAY carry a "fallback" data key, tried only when dataKey yields a mock or an error. None does right now. gold, sp500, nasdaq and oil each need one -- EIA publishes no gold series at all and the other three need API keys that are not set, so all four serve MOCK constants that code/market-collect.js correctly refuses, and they cannot accumulate an observation. code/providers/stooq-provider.js was written to be that fallback and is NOT wired in: its four symbol codes returned HTTP 404 when probed on the real machine on 2026-09-04, and an unverified source does not get to write history. Re-enabling is one line per instrument once `node code/providers/stooq-provider.js --probe` reports 4 of 4.
_instruments: The only tradeable symbols. Anything else is refused. dataKey maps to the existing data layer -- these six are already served by code/providers/. Stop distances are wider for the volatile instruments, which is why their position caps come out smaller: 20% stop on a 3% position loses the same 0.6% as an 8% stop on a 7.5% position.
